study type: Retrospective analysis and Cohort study (two-stage study)
exposure: Anatomical variations in the vascular bed
Features of blood supply to various parts of the birth canal
Proposed surgical hemostasis tactics (ligation of internal iliac arteries, local hemostasis, compression sutures, hysterectomy)
cohort: The study involved 255 pregnant women, including a retrospective analysis of 77 maternal deaths due to obstetric bleeding and a prospective cohort of 178 women who experienced bleeding during cesarean section and childbirth.
finding: One primary finding was that anatomical variations in the vascular bed and features of blood supply influence the development and progression of massive obstetric bleeding, and the implementation of a developed surgical hemostasis algorithm significantly decreased the frequency of massive obstetric bleeding, the number of hysterectomies, and the volume of blood loss.
